blocks.text: Imagine transferring money between bank accounts. What if a system crash occurs mid-transfer? The ACID properties ensure data integrity even in such scenarios.

blocks.markdown: In database systems, transactions are sequences of operations that perform a single logical function. To ensure data integrity and consistency, transactions must adhere to the ACID properties: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability. These properties protect against various failures, ensuring that databases remain reliable and accurate.

blocks.title: Atomicity
blocks.text: Atomicity ensures that a transaction is all-or-nothing. If any part of the transaction fails, the entire transaction is rolled back, leaving the database unchanged.

blocks.title: Consistency
blocks.text: Consistency ensures that a transaction takes the database from one valid state to another, maintaining all predefined rules, such as constraints, cascades, and triggers.

blocks.title: Isolation
blocks.text: Isolation ensures that concurrent transactions do not interfere with each other. Each transaction should appear as though it is the only one being executed at a time.

blocks.title: Durability
blocks.text: Durability guarantees that once a transaction is committed, it will remain so, even in the event of a system failure.

blocks.title: Atomicity in Action
blocks.prompt: Consider a transaction that transfers 100 dollars from Account A to Account B. What happens if the system crashes after debiting Account A but before crediting Account B?

steps.text: Initially, Account A has 500 dollars and Account B has 300 dollars.
The transaction begins by debiting 100 dollars from Account A, leaving it with 400 dollars.
Before crediting Account B, the system crashes.
Due to atomicity, the transaction is rolled back, restoring Account A to 500 dollars.

blocks.answer: The atomicity property ensures that the transaction is rolled back, leaving both accounts unchanged from their initial state.

blocks.title: Key Point
blocks.text: Atomicity protects against partial updates, ensuring that transactions are fully completed or not executed at all.

blocks.title: Consistency Example
blocks.prompt: A database has a constraint that the total balance of all accounts must be non-negative. How does consistency ensure this during a transaction?

steps.text: Consider two accounts with balances of 500 dollars and -200 dollars, respectively.
A transaction attempts to transfer 400 dollars from the first account to the second.
This would leave the first account with 100 dollars and the second with 200 dollars.
Since the total balance is still positive, the transaction is consistent with the database rules.

blocks.answer: Consistency ensures that the transaction maintains the rule that the total balance remains non-negative.

blocks.caption: ACID properties and their corresponding failure protections.

blocks.markdown: Understanding the ACID properties is crucial for designing robust database systems. Each property addresses specific types of failures, ensuring that transactions are reliable and data integrity is maintained.

points: ACID properties are essential for data integrity in databases.
Consistency maintains database rules and constraints.
Isolation prevents interference from concurrent transactions.
Durability ensures committed transactions persist despite failures.
